questions.question: Which method is used to initialize the Braze Web SDK with an API key and configuration?
questions.explanation: The correct method is braze.initialize(apiKey, config). This sets up the Web SDK with your API key and optional configuration options.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'baseUrl' parameter in the Braze Web SDK initialization?
options: It specifies the Braze API endpoint for your instance
It sets the domain for cookies
questions.explanation: The baseUrl parameter specifies the Braze API endpoint for your specific instance (e.g., 'https://sdk.iad-01.braze.com'). This is required for proper SDK communication.

questions.question: True or False: The changeUser() method must be called before openSession() to ensure user identification.
questions.explanation: Yes, if you have a logged-in user, changeUser() should be called before openSession() to ensure the session and subsequent events are associated with the correct user profile.

questions.question: Which method is called to enable automatic display of in-app messages in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The braze.automaticallyShowInAppMessages() method enables automatic display of in-app messages. Without this call, in-app messages won't display automatically.

questions.question: True or False: When using changeUser(), any sessions or events logged before the call will automatically be attributed to the new user.
questions.explanation: No, sessions and events logged before changeUser() are attributed to the previous user. changeUser() only affects subsequent sessions and events.

questions.question: How do you set a custom attribute on a user in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax is braze.getUser().setCustomUserAttribute('key', value). This retrieves the current user and sets a custom attribute on their profile.

questions.question: Which method is used to log a custom event in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct method is braze.logCustomEvent(eventName, properties). The properties parameter is optional but allows you to pass additional event data.

questions.question: True or False: The Braze Web SDK automatically handles service worker registration for push notifications.
questions.explanation: Yes, by default, the Web SDK automatically registers and manages the service worker when requestPushPermission() is called or at the start of each new session for users with push permission.

questions.question: What does the requestPushPermission() method do in the Braze Web SDK?
options: It enables push notifications on the SDK
It checks if push is already enabled
It requests browser push notification permission from the user
It registers the device for push notifications
questions.explanation: The requestPushPermission() method prompts the user to grant push notification permission in their browser. This should typically be called in response to a user action.

questions.question: True or False: You can use the 'allowUserSuppliedJavascript' initialization option to enable custom JavaScript in in-app messages.
questions.explanation: Yes, setting allowUserSuppliedJavascript: true allows in-app messages to execute custom JavaScript that has been configured in the Braze dashboard.

questions.question: Which method retrieves the currently logged-in user object in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The braze.getUser() method returns the current user object, which you can then use to set attributes, emails, and other user properties.

questions.question: How do you log a purchase event in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct method is braze.logPurchase(productId, price, currency, properties). This logs a purchase event with optional properties.

questions.question: True or False: The sessionTimeoutInSeconds initialization option controls how long a user can be inactive before their session ends.
questions.explanation: Yes, the sessionTimeoutInSeconds option (default 30 minutes) specifies the inactivity period after which a new session is started for the user.

questions.question: Which of the following is the recommended way to integrate the Braze Web SDK?
options: By copying and pasting the SDK code
questions.explanation: NPM integration is recommended because it stores SDK libraries locally, provides protection from ad-blockers, and enables faster load times with bundler support.

questions.question: True or False: You must manually set the 'deviceId' during initialization if you want to track anonymous users.
questions.explanation: No, the Braze Web SDK automatically generates a device ID for anonymous users. You only need to set a custom deviceId if you have a specific requirement.

questions.question: What method is used to request an immediate data flush to the Braze servers in the Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The braze.requestImmediateDataFlush() method forces the SDK to immediately send queued data to Braze servers instead of waiting for the regular sync interval.

questions.question: True or False: The Web SDK automatically ignores activity from known web crawlers and spiders.
questions.explanation: Yes, by default, the Web SDK ignores activity from known spiders/crawlers (like Google, Bing) based on the user agent string. This saves data points and improves analytics accuracy.

questions.question: How do you subscribe to content card updates in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct method is braze.subscribeToContentCardsUpdates(callback). This registers a callback that fires whenever content cards are updated.

questions.question: True or False: To enable SDK Authentication in the Web SDK, you must set the enableSdkAuthentication option to true during initialization.
questions.explanation: Yes, SDK Authentication requires setting enableSdkAuthentication: true during initialization. This adds an additional layer of security to prevent unauthorized SDK requests.

questions.question: What does the 'manageServiceWorkerExternally' initialization option do?
options: It allows you to manage your own service worker instead of letting Braze manage it
It forces the SDK to create a new service worker
It enables automatic service worker updates
questions.explanation: Setting manageServiceWorkerExternally: true allows you to manage your own service worker and integrate Braze push functionality into it, rather than letting the SDK manage it.

questions.question: How do you set standard user attributes like email and first name in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax is braze.getUser().setEmail(...) and braze.getUser().setFirstName(...). These methods set standard attributes on the current user profile.

questions.question: True or False: By default, the Web SDK will automatically sync a user's push token on each new session if they already granted push permission.
questions.explanation: Yes, the Web SDK automatically syncs push tokens on new sessions for users who previously granted push permission, unless you set disablePushTokenMaintenance: true.

questions.question: Which method is used to request Content Cards refresh from the Braze server in the Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct method is braze.requestContentCardsRefresh(). This sends a background request to fetch the latest Content Cards from the Braze server.

questions.question: True or False: You must remove the automaticallyShowInAppMessages() call if you want to implement soft push prompts.
questions.explanation: Yes, for soft push prompts, you must remove automaticallyShowInAppMessages() and instead use subscribeToInAppMessage() to handle custom push primer messages.

questions.question: What is the purpose of calling openSession() in the Braze Web SDK?
options: To authenticate the user with a password
To start tracking a new user session
To connect to the Braze server
questions.explanation: The openSession() method starts tracking a new user session. It should be called after initialization, changeUser(), and automaticallyShowInAppMessages().

questions.question: True or False: The Web SDK automatically removes test campaign cards received from the Content Cards test send feature when receiving Content Cards updates.
questions.explanation: No, as of recent versions, test cards are no longer removed when the SDK receives Content Cards updates, allowing you to keep test cards visible while developing.

questions.question: How do you set a custom location attribute in the Braze Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax uses setCustomLocationAttribute() for each location dimension. Standard attributes like country are set with setCountry(), etc.

questions.question: True or False: The inAppMessageZIndex initialization option controls the z-index of in-app messages on the page.
questions.explanation: Yes, the inAppMessageZIndex option (default 999999) specifies the z-index for in-app messages, allowing you to control layering with other page elements.

questions.question: Which method allows you to manually log a Content Card click in the Web SDK?
questions.explanation: The correct method is braze.logCardClick(card). This logs a click for the specified Content Card object.

questions.question: True or False: In the Web SDK, you can use nested custom attributes and arrays of objects with the setCustomUserAttribute() method.
questions.explanation: Yes, setCustomUserAttribute() supports nested custom attributes and arrays of objects, with an optional merge parameter to control how values are updated.
